tagline: Running out of drugs that haven't already failed me.
paragraph: I've been struggling for years to find something that works, minus one good two-year stretch I keep trying to get back to. The list of what I've tried reads like a pharmacy shelf — plaquenil that honestly isn't doing anything, six months of cyclophosphamide back in 2020, Gazyva starting in January after I relapsed, Benlysta a few weeks in with no improvement yet. One neurologist put me on a medicine for trigeminal neuralgia that swelled my face until my eyes nearly popped out, and the damage put me back to square one. I switched to a rheumatologist at USC Keck hoping for new ideas and was told that since my kidneys 'seem fine,' my only option is hydroxychloroquine. I have lupus nephritis class 4 and have been told I'm not a candidate for remission — expect to be on meds the rest of my life. So a two-year treatment plan actually sounds good to me. Right now I'm in a huge flare, back on prednisone, nothing tastes good, I can barely walk, and I'm widowed raising our 11-year-old on my own. I fought through dialysis as hard as I could to get this kidney back so I could be the parent and the hard worker I used to be. The doctors are 'excited' because what they're trying next hasn't been done before. I don't feel excited. I feel exhausted. This has to get better — I don't know how the hell I'm going to manage if it doesn't.
patient_concerns: Exhausted the standard biologics and the one I tolerate barely works anymore.
Switching rheumatologists hoping for new options and being told plaquenil is it.
Bad reactions and side effects — swelling, hair loss, nausea needing ER Zofran drips.
Being told I'm not a candidate for remission, just lifelong immunosuppression.
person_concerns: Want to be the parent and worker I was before my kidneys shut down.
Raising my kid alone while I can barely walk and have no energy.
Grieving the two-year stretch when treatment actually worked and life felt normal.
Scared the doctors are guessing and I'm the experiment they're excited about.
